title: Freya and the Locker
premise: In the fading mill town of Halloway Bend, Zephyrine Ishikawa has perfected invisibility — until his best friend Theo vanishes overnight, leaving behind a locker key and a trail of coded notes. Following them, Zeph discovers Theo was investigating the town's drowned history and a secret circle of kids who've been quietly documenting everyone's hidden selves, including Zeph's. As suspicion falls on Zeph and the search turns desperate, he must choose between protecting his own secrets and saving Theo, who is trapped in the flooded quarry with a broken leg. The book ends with Zeph coming out to the whole town at the rescue's edge — not as a confession, but as a refusal to hide anymore — and with Theo found alive, both boys forever changed by what they were willing to risk for each other.
about_author: Mirabel Delacroix is the pen name of a former small-town librarian who spent a decade watching teenagers find refuge in the stacks. She writes stories about quiet kids in loud places and lives near a lake that freezes too early every year.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Neighbors
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV establishes his careful choreography of invisibility in Halloway Bend: the head-down walks, the grades, the locked locker as metaphor and fact. A small moment with Theo hints at deeper friendship. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety.

chapters.title: The Last Normal Tuesday
chapters.summary: Theo acts strange after school, pressing a spare key into Zeph's hand and saying 'if I'm not here tomorrow, don't look for me — look for what I left.' POV alternates briefly to Theo's journal fragment. Beat: dread blooming under ordinary light.

chapters.title: Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Theo doesn't show up. Police canvass; the town performs concern while whispering about Theo's family. Zeph hides the key from investigators, terrified it implicates him. Beat: guilt and fear entwining.

chapters.title: What the Key Opens
chapters.summary: Alone at night, Zeph tries the key on school lockers and finds it opens locker 114 — long abandoned, containing Theo's notebook of coded entries about the quarry and something called 'the Ledger.' Beat: the pull of secrets stronger than fear.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Deciphering the code, Zeph learns Theo belonged to a loose group of five students who documented the town's buried truths — including an entry about Zeph himself, tender and unjudged. Beat: exposed, but strangely seen.

chapters.title: Five Names
chapters.summary: Zeph tracks down two other members: Priya, hostile and grieving, and Marcus, scared into silence by his father, a town councilman. They reveal Theo was close to proving the quarry flood that killed three workers decades ago was covered up. Beat: alliance forged in distrust.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Deputy Voss questions Zeph about the key; his evasiveness makes him a suspect. His mother's fear and fierce love surface. Beat: the cost of secrecy begins outweighing its protection.

chapters.title: Quarry Water
chapters.summary: Zeph and Priya explore the quarry rim and find fresh rope marks and Theo's jacket. Someone else has been there recently. Beat: hope curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Circle Breaks
chapters.summary: Marcus's father discovers the Ledger copies and forces Marcus to hand them over; the group splinters. Priya accuses Zeph of caring more about his own secrets than Theo. Beat: betrayal and self-recognition.

chapters.title: Entry Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: A hidden final journal page reveals Theo went to the quarry alone to retrieve physical proof — and that he'd planned to come out publicly alongside Zeph, so neither would stand alone. Beat: devastating tenderness; Zeph understands Theo's disappearance may be accident, not flight.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Voices
chapters.summary: The town organizes a search; Zeph must decide whether to share what he knows and expose the Ledger. He gives Deputy Voss everything except one page. Beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: Flood Season
chapters.summary: Rain swells the quarry. Zeph realizes the rising water will drown any trace — or anyone trapped below. He and Priya race the weather to retrace Theo's route through the old maintenance tunnel. Beat: ticking clock made literal.

chapters.title: Locked In
chapters.summary: Inside the tunnel, they find Theo's flashlight still wedged in a grate over a lower chamber. A faint tapping answers their calls. Beat: terror and elation colliding.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: They discover evidence of the cover-up — unsigned documents implicating the councilman and the mill owner — and realize someone from town followed Theo down. Footsteps above them. Beat: the past is not past.

chapters.title: Trapped
chapters.summary: The tunnel entrance floods behind them, stranding all three searchers. Zeph's phone dies mid-call to 911. Beat: claustrophobic despair; the rescuers need rescuing.

chapters.title: What Zeph Is Afraid Of
chapters.summary: Huddled in the dark waiting for water to recede, Zeph confesses to Priya everything — his identity, his years of hiding, why Theo's note gutted him. Beat: the true climax is internal; honesty as survival.

chapters.title: Rescue Line
chapters.summary: Dawn brings rescuers; the extraction is harrowing, and Theo is pulled from the lower chamber alive but hypothermic. The crowd on the ridge includes the whole town — and cameras. Beat: relief shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: Locker 114, Opened
chapters.summary: At the hospital, Theo wakes; the boys' reunion is quiet and complete. But the recovered documents are now public, and the councilman spins the story to paint Theo as a trespasser. Beat: victory threatened by narrative war.

chapters.title: The Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: At the town meeting meant to discredit Theo, Zeph stands up, tells the truth about the cover-up — and about himself, plainly, without apology. Silence, then Priya stands, then others. Beat: catharsis; belonging claimed, not granted.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: An investigation reopens; consequences land unevenly, and some neighbors turn cold. Zeph grieves the version of home he lost and discovers a smaller, truer one. Beat: bittersweet realism.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Theo returns to school. He and Zeph open locker 114 together and leave the Ledger inside for whoever needs it next, adding a new first page. Beat: legacy and continuity.

chapters.title: Head Up
chapters.summary: Final chapter mirrors chapter one: same walk to school, transformed. Zeph greets people by name, locker shut but no longer locked. Closing beat: identity as choice, memory as foundation, belonging as practice.
